page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 60.0 GB of system memory. The hardware configuration includes a bundled 472 GB local SSD and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Pascal-generation P100 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance split between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated operations. The Intel Xeon CPU delivers weak to poor performance in general-purpose compute tests, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 10% and multi-core in the bottom 25%. Similarly, memory bandwidth and database operations underperform, with PassMark database and Redis SET operations ranking in the bottom 25%. However, the integrated NVIDIA P100 GPU excels in machine learning tasks, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing and text generation for medium-sized models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a specialized resource allocation where value is concentrated in the GPU and bundled local SSD storage rather than raw CPU compute density. It is poorly suited for CPU-heavy compilation, cryptography, or high-throughput database hosting. Instead, the ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is best utilized for GPU-accelerated workloads such as medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning model evaluation, and parallel processing tasks that can offload computation from the host CPU.
